analysis: The two supplied units are BASE-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (base lines 1649-2242), which are historical release notes for versions v0.9.x and earlier. The only change in this PR file is documentation: a new v0.10.1 candidate section is added at head lines 11-151, replacing the v0.10.0 header at base lines 11-13. That head content is not in the supplied units, only a truncated patch excerpt. The excerpt does not change security controls. Within the excerpt, the stated operational notes are: a recommended coordinator companion (darkbloom-platform#411) that refuses logprobs on certain models, a submodule pin move of libs/mlx-swift-lm with no Metal kernel changes, and page-cache accounting changes affecting load admission and KV budgets. The supplied BASE text shows no code or configuration changes and no secrets. I raise no finding. Remaining uncertainty: the page-cache accounting change in the truncated patch could affect memory admission and availability (T-029, T-010 class), and the mlx-swift-lm pin update could affect TB-007 inference behavior. Both are documented only in the changelog; the underlying source files are not in this batch, so their security effect is unverified and belongs to the source-code review of the corresponding files. T-041 (prefix cache) cache TTL and disk-budget statements in the base changelog are consistent with the canonical model and unchanged by the visible excerpt. The excerpt's claim that GLM logprob groundwork stays disabled should be checked against the actual code, and a version-gating or coordinator-dependency mismatch (a 0.10.0 provider failing a request with a 500 that cools every provider of the model) is documented as a rollout risk, not a new regression in this diff.
